backlog.spec: In solve, keep the 30% random-restart phase as is, but in the refinement phase track a separate 'current' packing in addition to the global 'best'. Perturb 'current' (pass it as start), and accept into 'current' only if the sum of radii improves, as now. Count consecutive non-improving hops; when the count reaches 25, reset 'current' by running fresh random restarts (start=None) 4 times and taking the best of those 4 as the new 'current', then reset the counter. Always update the global 'best' whenever any repaired packing beats it, and return the global best. No other change.
backlog.title: Stagnation restart with independent walkers

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that places circles one at a time. For each new circle, sample about 2000 candidate points uniformly in [0,1]^2 with the seed rng, and pick the candidate maximising its clearance, defined as the minimum of the distance to every placed centre minus that centre's radius and the distance to the walls. Set the new circle's radius to that clearance, capped at 0.2. Use the resulting centres and radii as x0 for SLSQP in place of the uniform random start, for about 50% of explore restarts. This produces a feasible, well-spread start and replaces the purely random draw.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-clearance sequential initialization

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision vector before calling SLSQP. Scale the centre coordinates and radii by a fixed factor of 10 (or divide by 1/n-based scale), so that the variables and constraint values have comparable magnitudes. Pass the objective as minus the scaled radius sum. Unscale the result before repair. Keep every constraint and the iteration limit unchanged, so only the conditioning of the QP subproblems changes. Check that the final repaired packings are valid under the 1e-10 harness tolerance.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning

backlog.spec: In solve, change the explore condition from 0.3 * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit to 0.4 * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit, so more fresh random restarts are made before refinement starts. A 15% phase scored worse (slot 33), so this tests the other direction. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Explore phase at 40% instead of 30%

backlog.spec: For a fraction of explore restarts (say 40%), solve _solve_once for n+1 circles from the same rng, then delete the circle with the smallest final radius, and pass the remaining n centres and radii through the repair step. Keep the normal n-circle path for the rest. The extra circle gives SLSQP room to rearrange, and dropping the weakest one tends to leave a different, feasible basin. No other logic changes.
backlog.title: Over-populate and prune starts

backlog.spec: In solve, replace the fixed stop condition 'elapsed < TIME_FRACTION * time_limit' by an adaptive guard: record the CPU time of each _solve_once + _repair call, keep the maximum seen (longest), and continue looping while elapsed + 1.5 * longest < 0.95 * time_limit (use longest = 2.0 s before the first call finishes). Keep the explore/refine switch at 0.3 * 0.8 * time_limit CPU seconds exactly as now. This uses the idle 20% tail for extra refinement hops while staying far below the 45 s void limit.
backlog.title: Adaptive time guard based on the longest observed run

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, in the relocate branch (rng.random() < 0.5), choose the circles to move from the smallest ones instead of uniformly: let k = rng.integers(2, 5), take the 2*k indices with the smallest r0 (via np.argsort) and pick k of them at random with rng.choice(..., k, replace=False). Give them uniform random centres and radius INIT_RADIUS*0.5 as now. Small circles are usually the badly placed ones, and moving them barely changes the main structure.
backlog.title: Relocate the smallest circles instead of random ones

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 30% explore split with a simple epsilon-greedy bandit over two arms, fresh random restart and perturbation of the current best. Each arm keeps a running mean of the improvement it gives to best.sum(). At each iteration pick the arm with probability 0.8 by highest mean and 0.2 uniformly at random, and update the chosen arm's mean after the call. Keep TIME_FRACTION unchanged. This lets the budget shift towards whichever move is paying off on the given seed.
backlog.title: Bandit allocation between explore and refine

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, remove the four wall-constraint blocks from cons. Pass bounds to SLSQP instead: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. The wall constraints c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 are then not enforced by bounds alone, so keep only the radius bound r>=0 as a bound. Keep the repair step as it is. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds up each SLSQP run, so more refinement steps fit in the time budget.
backlog.title: Walls as variable bounds

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, in the warm-start branch, change the move probability from rng.random() < 0.5 to rng.random() < 0.7 for the relocate move, and relocate rng.integers(1, 3) circles (1 or 2) instead of rng.integers(2, 5). Keep the shake branch and everything else as it is. Smaller relocations disturb the incumbent less and so are more often accepted.
backlog.title: Fewer relocated circles, more often

backlog.spec: After the main loop ends, spend about 1 s of CPU, which means reducing TIME_FRACTION slightly to 0.77. Run SLSQP from the best packing (centres and radii, with radii scaled by 0.999) with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-12. Repair it and keep it only if the radius sum is larger than the best sum.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of best packing

backlog.spec: Track the best sum of radii over explore restarts. If the last K=8 fresh random starts have not improved best by more than 1e-4, switch from the explore phase to the perturbation phase at once, instead of waiting for the fixed 30% of TIME_FRACTION. Otherwise continue exploring until the time cutoff. Keep the existing perturbation and acceptance code unchanged. The point is to spend time where restarts have stopped paying off.
backlog.title: Stall-triggered switch to refinement

backlog.spec: Take the incumbent slot 9 perturbation and change the centre-noise sd choice to be drawn per hop from a log-uniform distribution over [0.003, 0.03]. For the relocation move, relocate 1 to 2 circles instead of 2 to 4. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Perturbation size tuning

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, the jitter branch of the perturbation uses a fixed centre-noise sd of 0.02. Replace the fixed sd with one drawn per call from a log-uniform distribution on [0.004, 0.06]: sd = 0.004 * (15 ** rng.random()), then c0 = c0 + rng.normal(0, sd, c0.shape). Leave the relocate branch, the 50/50 branch split, the greedy acceptance in solve and all other settings unchanged. This is not the adaptive feedback scheme of slot 17: the sd is sampled independently each call, with no state.
backlog.title: Log-uniform noise scale in the jitter move

backlog.spec: In solve, during the refinement phase (after the explore phase), with probability 0.15 per iteration pass start=None to _solve_once (a fresh random restart) instead of the best packing. Use rng.random() < 0.15 to decide. Keep the acceptance rule as it is: the result is kept only if its repaired sum beats best. This keeps some diversity in case the refinement is stuck in a poor basin.
backlog.title: Occasional fresh restart during refinement

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, in the branch where a start is given and the shake move is chosen (the else branch), change the centre noise from rng.normal(0, 0.02, c0.shape) to rng.normal(0, 0.01, c0.shape). Change nothing else. The aim is to see whether smaller kicks stay in good basins more often, which tunes the slot 9 incumbent's perturbation size.
backlog.title: Smaller centre noise in the shake move

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, build the initial radii instead of using np.full(n, INIT_RADIUS): draw a random permutation of the n circles and give 4 of them radius 0.12, 12 of them 0.09 and the rest 0.06. Keep the uniform random centres. Leave the warm-start branch and solve() unchanged. This combines the weakly positive slot 4 start with the slot 9 explore-then-refine schedule.
backlog.title: Size-class radii for fresh starts on top of the refinement incumbent

backlog.spec: Only for fresh random starts in _solve_once (start is None), replace the uniform initial radius INIT_RADIUS with size classes: after drawing the random centres, sort circles by distance of their centre to the nearest corner of the square, give the 4 closest r=0.13, the next 12 r=0.10 and the remaining n-16 r=0.07, then multiply all initial radii by 0.6 so the start is not badly overlapping. Leave the refinement phase (start from best, relocate/jitter) completely unchanged. This combines the weakly positive slot 4 start with the slot 9 incumbent.
backlog.title: Size-class radii for explore-phase starts

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, choose a random circle and its 4 nearest neighbours. Add centre noise of sd 0.03 only to those 5 circles and shrink their radii by 0.5. Then run the full SLSQP. This perturbs one local cluster while the rest of the packing keeps its structure.
backlog.title: Refinement restricted to active-neighbour shake

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the global jitter branch with a cluster rotation with probability 0.5 of the times that branch is taken (the other times keep the sd 0.02 jitter). Pick a random circle i, take all circles whose centre lies within 0.28 of centre i, compute the centroid g of that cluster, and rotate the cluster centres about g by an angle drawn uniformly from [-pi/3, pi/3] (excluding nothing; small angles are fine). Clip centres to [0, 1] and start those cluster radii at 0.7 * r0 and the other radii at 0.9 * r0. Everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation move

memo:
Helped: only slot 9 (30% random restarts, then perturbing the best packing with an acceptance rule): -2.6360, delta -0.0080, about 3.5 noise sd. It is a single run and has not been replicated, so it may be luck. Near misses, within noise of slot 9: slot 17 adaptive sd (-2.6354) and slot 28 walker (-2.6350). Weakly positive: slot 4 size-class start (-0.0024).

Did not help: SLSQP speed-ups and constraint forms (slots 0, 1, 2, 11), TIME_FRACTION 0.9, LP refit, staged jitter, remove-and-reinsert, short-iteration screening, alternative starts (sum r^p, Beta, lattice, pre-relaxation), swap and crossover moves, elite pools (+0.0092), always shaking (+0.0120), longer refinement maxiter, top-3 basin-hopping, and a 15% explore phase (-2.6318).

Next: 1) replicate slot 9 to confirm it. 2) Tune its perturbation size and restart fraction. 3) Combine it with the slot 4 start. 4) Skip micro-optimisations and further start-generation ideas.
